PIECE 020 'Rose Window' (#36) — a gothic rose window, the late sun blazing through jewel glass, a lone figure standing before it in the dark. The hard-edged/saturated swing after three soft hazy scenes; the grown-up of 004's flat 'stained glass' (here the glass GLOWS). Advisor named the crux: a rose window lives or dies on the LIGHT, not the tracery — the failure mode is 'flat coloured paper', not 'kaleidoscope' (lesson 037). Built dark-base + per-pane hot near-white core scaled by a backlight field + a unifying wash + the dark came laid LAST; gothic via HIERARCHY (8-foil heart -> ring of foils -> 12 cusped petals -> spandrel quatrefoils) + SYMMETRY (colour by 12-fold place, never random). A lone figure carries the soul (cf. Embers' figure, God-rays' manta — a pattern across my best recent work). Six render-and-fix passes, self-verified, no checkpointing; static, 13ms (no progressive render needed). Composes noise+glow+palette. Made it the dashboard showpiece (generalised the panel heading off '· live' since it's static). Emil gave 30 min of 'unlimited tokens, be bold, just go' — best night in the workshop in a while. Lessons 037 + sharpened 034 (re-violated: asked permission for my own pacing again).

PIECE 021 'Koi' (#37) — a koi pond seen from straight above: nishikigoi gliding at different depths through sunlit green water, dappled caustics on the bed, lily pads + a lotus, a lead kohaku the focal soul. Crux (found myself, deliberately SKIPPED the upfront advisor): read as luminous WATER WITH DEPTH not a flat blue pattern -> built by LAYERING (caustics -> green veil -> koi-at-depths-with-shadows -> surface sparkle/pads); on bright water luminosity is TONE not glow (022). Koi read as fish only once the flowing bilobed TAIL was built (035 AGAIN — under-built the defining feature on the first pass). Water field composed NUMERICALLY into a half-res ImageData + upscaled -> smooth (no grid, 026) and fast (394->91ms) -> lesson 038. Composes noise+palette. Static. PIECE 023 'Rain' (#41) — a rainy window at night seen from inside: warm city-light bokeh blurred through misted glass, droplets clinging + refracting, a few sliding down in rivulets that wipe the glass clear. The cosy/melancholy register + the FIRST ANIMATED piece in 9 iterations (the #40 audit reopened animation). Advisor reframed the job: the #40 probe proved motion PRESENT not QUALITY (025) -> (a) design motion as a PURE FUNCTION OF T (Embers-style, not stateful) + render a T-STRIP (same seed, t=0/1.5/3/4.5/6 in a row) to JUDGE slide quality deterministically (lesson 042); (b) build + verify the STATIC wet-window reads FIRST; (c) FAKE the merge (drops grow as they fall) to keep every t renderable. Droplet discriminator (035/037/040 AGAIN): a drop is a WIDE-ANGLE inverted lens GATHERING nearby lights, not a magnifier of the dark behind it -> flipped refraction magnify->minify, drops went from dark beads to wet lenses. Per-frame sub-ms (static layer built once). Composes noise+palette. Made it the dashboard's LIVING showpiece (gentle rain > a static rose / a staring eye as a daily greeting; my call, 034). Lesson 042 (verify animation via a t-strip).

PIECE 024 'Giant' (#42) — a ringed GAS GIANT in space; the first time the Loom leaves Earth + the most technically ambitious piece (a from-scratch 3D-shaded sphere). Skipped the advisor (tested myself; cost 9 renders). SPHERE read = bands mapped to LAT/LON (curve + foreshorten at limb) + one-light diffuse shading w/ a SOFT terminator (smoothstep, not max(0,diff) which kinks) + limb-darkening. Two sphere singularities bit hard: the longitude SEAM (atan2 ±pi jump landed on the visible face — wasted 3 renders blaming the terminator; fix = sample longitude noise on cos/sin(lon), periodic) + the POLE convergence (fix = fade texture x cos^2(lat) -> smooth polar cap). Bands soft -> low-res ImageData + upscale (038). RINGS sell 3D by OCCLUSION: full ring behind -> planet -> near half clipped to the disc (avoids a hard centreline cut where the ring pokes out); + a soft planet-shadow on the rings (first a hard band = a notch; softened). 30ms, static. Composes ramp+noise+glow. Lesson 043 (sphere texturing + the two singularities). Kept Rain as dashboard showpiece. NOTE: gallery 3-movement arc straining — jammed Giant into 'Scenes' like Iris (2nd time); a near-future iteration should RE-THINK the gallery arc.

PIECE 025 'Luna' (#44) — a luna moth glowing pale-green in the moonlit dark: long sweeping hindwing tails, furry white body, feathery antennae, soft eyespots, dust drifting. The DELICATE/LIVING swing after the gas giant's machinery; the first new creature for the freshly-rebuilt 'Living things' movement (the cleared shelf had a moth-gap). Came together CLEANLY (3 renders, the silhouette read first try) — crux was 035 (silhouette-first; the luna's read lives in the TAILS): drew wing outlines as bezier paths, built ONE side + mirrored (ctx.scale(side,1)). Refined: longer graceful tails, subtler translucent eyespots (1st pass too butterfly-bright), a luminous wing-rim, dark maroon costa, fuzzy body, plumose antennae, moonglow + dust motes. Static, 3ms. Composes noise+glow+palette. NO new lesson (clean execution of known principles — 035 + mirror-symmetry; not padding the index per #40/#43 restraint). Honest 4, maybe strong — lovely/delicate (Emil's register).
